messages:
Incident Bot: paging oncall: node node-usw2-7 reporting nodefs.available < 2% and multiple kubelet eviction events on model-serving pods :rotating_light:
ops-pager: oncall Lia OConnor (infra) — please investigate, customer-facing errors seen in prod.
Lia OConnor: acked — jumping in. any immediate customer impact? which stacks affected?
Alex K: seeing a spike in OOMs and a bunch of `CrashLoopBackOff` for runtime pods on that node. modelcache pods log shows repeated write errors.
Maria P: customer-facing app shows 502s for a subset of requests routed to that node, correlated with model-serving route.
Sanjay R: attaching short log snip from one runtime pod: ``ERROR: failed to persist shard /tmp/modelcache/shard_23: write: no space left on device``
Alex K: also seeing a lot of debug logging filling /tmp because someone accidentally left `LOG_LEVEL=debug` on the runtime cronjob that writes checkpoints to local tmpdir.
Lia OConnor: going to `kubectl get pods -o wide` and `df -h` on node. pls hold on.
Lia OConnor: node shows /var/lib/kubelet and /tmp at 99% usage. multiple modelcache pods on that node with huge log files: `/var/log/pods/*/modelcache/*.log` > 20GB each.
ops-pager: add `@sanjay` for modelcache context — did we recently change checkpoint frequency or enable WAL?
Sanjay R: recent change: WAL enabled for the LRU cache to speed restart recovery (PR #4121). It rotates but I didn't expect the debug-level logs to sync so frequently.
Alex K: immediate mitigation idea: cordon the node, drain non-critical pods, and rotate logs / compress. we should also disable WAL or set it to lower sync frequency for in-flight recovery.
Maria P: customers impacted: a few workspace tenants showing degraded generation latency and 5% error rate on hosted API. Not widespread but visible on dashboards.
Lia OConnor: cordoning node now: `kubectl cordon node-usw2-7` — done.
Lia OConnor: trying `kubectl drain node-usw2-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` — some pods blocked because they have local-only data (modelcache).
Alex K: for modelcache pods we need a graceful evacuation: scale up a replacement node or schedule new pods onto different nodes by setting nodeAffinity/taints.
Sanjay R: quick patch: set WAL sync interval to 30s and restart modelcache pods on healthy nodes. I'll push config to k8s configmap and rollout.
Maria P: ops: can we reduce log verbosity on the runtime containers? Spotting `trace`/`debug` lines filling disk.
Lia OConnor: I can truncate the largest logs on the node: `for f in $(ls -S /var/log/pods/*/modelcache/*.log | head -n 10); do : > $f; done` — executing now.
Incident Bot: deploybot: rolling update of modelcache-config started by S. R (PR 4129)
Sanjay R: rolled out config update to namespace `prod-models` — WAL interval bumped, debug->info. Waiting for new pods to schedule.
Alex K: noticed after log truncation, kubelet freed enough space to stop immediate evictions but some pods already crashed with CUDA init errors. sample error:
```
[2025-07-02T13:47:02Z] runtime: CUDA driver: failed to initialize device 0: cuInit error: device unavailable
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "serve.py", line 142, in start
    ctx = cuda.Context(0)
RuntimeError: CUDA initialization failed: no devices found
```
Maria P: that looks like the pod lost GPU assignment during eviction/recreate. Need to ensure GPU device plugin is healthy and that pod scheduling preserves GPU assignment.
Lia OConnor: checking node status: kubelet reports `eviction` events and docker reported `containerd: IO timeout` earlier. Could be IO hang.
ops-pager: recommend marking node unschedulable and reprovisioning; meanwhile move traffic off.
Alex K: implemented temporary route fallback: add model variant `small-quant` to fallback routes for the affected model to reduce risk while we heal. That should cut latency and avoid heavy modelcache writes.
Sanjay R: new modelcache pods on nodes node-usw2-9 and node-usw2-10 came up healthy. Verified they load shards and WAL is less chatty.
Lia OConnor: reprovisioning node-usw2-7 (reboot + kernel scrub) to clear stale fd/inotify leak and rotate logs.
Maria P: I've notified Customer Success and triage: affected tenants list: tenant-44, tenant-21, and a workspace customer (cid-1984). CS post sent with mitigation steps and ETA.
Alex K: long-term followups to capture in postmortem: - make WAL adaptive to available disk space - add alert for unexpected log growth per pod - ensure runtime doesn't write heavy checkpointing to ephemeral local tmpdir unless PVC present - add preemptive throttling on debug logs - add k8s PodDisruptionBudget for critical model-serving pods
Sanjay R: I'll open a follow-up ticket to add PVC-backed model cache option and an autoscale rule to spin up replacement nodes before eviction thresholds.
Lia OConnor: node reprovision done and back in cluster; draining completed earlier. marking incident as in mitigation.
Incident Bot: Incident status: mitigation in progress; severity reduced. Next: run post-incident blameless review in 48h.
ops-pager: thanks all. final checklist: confirm no further OOMs for 2h, validate GPU plugin health, confirm logs rotated and WAL behavior stable.
Maria P: monitoring hooks added to dashboards for the affected models and tenants. will reconvene if error rate creeps back up.
Alex K: thanks team — taking the followups. I'll put a short runbook entry for tmpdir quota leakage and debug log killswitch.
Lia OConnor: handing back to oncall rotation. Lia OConnor: resolved for now.
ops-pager: oncall handoff to next: @Alex K acknowledged and will track followups. :white_check_mark:
